The young man would formally put aside his childhood toga praetexta (with its purple border) and don the toga virilis, signifying his new status as a citizen with full legal rights and responsibilities. Skill:Skill 1.G: Identify stylistic features in Latin poetry and prose.
q.ex: Asyndeton is a rhetorical device in which conjunctions are deliberately omitted from a series of related clauses or phrases. In line 10 "Nulla... muta," the construction presents multiple elements without connecting words like "et" (and) or "que" (and). This creates a more rapid, emphatic effect by listing items in succession without the usual conjunctions that would normally link them in Latin prose. The absence of these connecting words between the elements is the defining characteristic of asyndeton, making it the figure of speech present in this line.

q.ex: The form "irascere" is a present imperative, specifically the second person singular present passive imperative of the deponent verb "irascor" (to be angry). Deponent verbs have passive forms but active meanings, so "irascere" means "be angry!" as a command directed at one person. The -re ending is characteristic of the present passive imperative singular for second and third conjugation verbs. This form functions as a direct command in the present tense, which is why it is classified as present imperative rather than an infinitive (which would be "irasci"), a perfect indicative, or a future indicative.

q.ex: The form "iunxero" is future perfect tense. In Latin, the future perfect is formed by adding the future tense endings of "esse" to the perfect stem. The "-ero" ending is the distinctive first person singular future perfect marker, as opposed to "-i" for perfect or "-eram" for pluperfect. The future perfect tense indicates an action that will have been completed before another future action or time. The correct answer is future perfect because "iunxero" uses the perfect stem "iunx-" plus the future perfect ending "-ero."

q.ex: Both "age" and "summitte" are imperative forms used to give commands or make requests. "Age" is an irregular imperative meaning "come" or "come now," while "summitte" is the plural imperative of "summitto" meaning "send down" or "lower." In Latin, the imperative mood is used to express direct commands, orders, or exhortations to the person or persons being addressed. These forms are neither indicative (stating facts), subjunctive (expressing possibility or purpose), nor infinitive (the base verb form). The correct answer is imperative because both verbs function as direct commands in the sentence.

q.ex: Metonymy is a figure of speech in which one word or phrase is substituted for another with which it is closely associated. In this case, "Martem" (Mars, the god of war) is used to represent war itself or military conflict. This is a classic example of metonymy because the deity associated with warfare stands in for the concept of war. The substitution works because Mars and war are so closely connected in Roman culture that the god's name naturally evokes the activity he represents. The correct answer is metonymy because the text uses the name of the god Mars to mean war or warfare.

The Latin word "vel" is a coordinating conjunction that functions as a disjunctive connector, meaning it presents alternatives or choices between two or more elements. q.ex: In Latin grammar, "mi amice" is in the vocative case, which is used specifically for direct address. The vocative case identifies the person or thing being spoken to directly. "Mi" is the vocative form of "meus" (my), and "amice" is the vocative singular of "amicus" (friend), together meaning "my friend" when calling out to or addressing someone. This construction does not indicate the subject performing an action, the object receiving an action, or an instrumental relationship, but rather marks the addressee of the speaker's words. The correct answer is that "mi amice" specifies who is being addressed.

The Senate was created as an advisory council of elders to help govern the new city, consisting initially of 100 patrician members. This institution became one of the most important and enduring features of Roman government, lasting throughout the Republic and into the Imperial period. The correct answer is senate because establishing this governing body was one of the foundational acts attributed to Rome's first ruler.

q.ex: The term "interregnum" comes from the Latin "inter" meaning "between" and "regnum" meaning "reign" or "rule." It specifically refers to the period when a throne is vacant between the death or departure of one ruler and the accession of the next. The other options refer to different Roman political concepts: "intercessio" was a veto power, "senatus consultum" was a decree of the Senate, and "comitia" were popular assemblies. The correct answer is "interregnum" because it literally means "between reigns" and precisely describes the transitional period of time without a ruler.

q.ex: The Latin phrase "annos undeviginti natus" translates literally as "having been born nineteen years" or more naturally as "being nineteen years old." The word "natus" is the perfect passive participle of "nascor" meaning "to be born," and when combined with an accusative of duration like "annos undeviginti" (nineteen years), it forms a standard Latin construction indicating age. The phrase describes Augustus himself at age nineteen, not the year of his birth or any sons. Therefore, the correct answer is that Augustus was nineteen years old.

 Itaque ad omnes casus subsidia comparabat. Nam et frumentum ex agris cotidie
 in castra conferebat et, quae gravissime adflictae erant naves, earum materia
5 atque aere ad reliquas reficiendas utebatur et quae ad eas res erant usui ex
 continenti comportari iubebat.

6. (A) Translate ad reliquas reficiendas (line 5) and (B) identify the grammatical construction.

At vero Aeneas aspectu obmutuit amens,
arrectaeque horrore comae et vox faucibus haesit.
Ardet abire fuga dulcesque relinquere terras,
attonitus tanto monitu imperioque deorum.
Heu quid agat? Quo nunc reginam ambire furentem
audeat adfatu? Quae prima exordia sumat
atque animum nunc huc celerem nunc dividit illuc
in partesque rapit varias perque omnia versat.
Haec alternanti potior sententia visa est.

4. Who had delivered to Aeneas the warning and command mentioned in line 4 ?

5. Translate in context the word alternanti (line 9).

6. (A) Translate in context the verb visa est (line 9) and (B) identify its tense.

     media nocte legionem proficisci celeriterque ad se venire. Exit cum nuntio Crassus.
      Alterum ad Gaium Fabium legatum mittit, ut in Atrebatium fines legionem adducat,

Apud Helvetios longe nobilissimus fuit et ditissimus Orgetorix. Is, M. Messala et
M. Pupio Pisone consulibus, regni cupiditate inductus coniurationem nobilitatis fecit
et civitati persuasit ut de finibus suis cum omnibus copiis exirent: perfacile esse, cum
virtute omnibus praestarent, totius Galliae imperio potiri. Id hoc facilius iis persuasit,
quod undique loci natura Helvetii continentur.

5. How long did M. Messala and M. Piso serve together as consuls?

 per superos et si qua fides tellure sub ima est:

Dido’s final struggle

q.ex: The Latin pronoun "illi" is the nominative plural form of "ille, illa, illud" meaning "those" or "they." In Latin grammar, the nominative case is used for the subject of a sentence, and the plural number indicates multiple persons or things. The form "illi" specifically refers to masculine or mixed-gender groups in the nominative case. This distinguishes it from "ille" (nominative singular), "illis" (dative/ablative plural), or other declined forms of the demonstrative pronoun. Therefore, nominative plural is correct because "illi" serves as the subject form referring to multiple entities.

q.ex: The form "audita" is a perfect passive participle in Latin, derived from the verb "audio, audire" (to hear). Perfect participles indicate completed action and are formed from the fourth principal part of the verb. In Latin, the perfect passive participle uses the stem "audit-" plus the appropriate ending (-a in this case, indicating feminine nominative or neuter nominative/accusative plural). This participle expresses an action that has been completed in the past, which is why it is classified as perfect tense. The correct answer is Perfect because "audita" represents the perfect passive participial form meaning "having been heard."

This crossing pattern is the defining characteristic of chiasmus, distinguishing it from simple parallelism. q.ex: Tyre was an ancient Phoenician city-state located on the eastern Mediterranean coast. The Phoenicians inhabited the coastal region of the Levant, in what is now modern-day Lebanon. Dido, the legendary founder and queen of Carthage, fled from Tyre after her brother Pygmalion killed her husband. The ancient city of Tyre still exists today as the city of Sour in southern Lebanon, making Lebanon the correct answer for the modern location of Dido's homeland.

q.ex: The gerund "fando" is the ablative form of the Latin gerund "fari" (to speak). The ablative case of a gerund typically expresses means or manner, answering the question "how" or "by what means." When translating an ablative gerund into English, it is most accurately rendered as "by" plus the present participle (the "-ing" form of the verb). Therefore, "fando" translates to "by speaking," indicating the means or manner by which an action is performed. The correct answer is "By speaking" because it properly reflects both the ablative case function and the gerund form.
